item.title: [planForChange] Power Platform – Information about the 2026 time zone changes in Canada
item.description:
What and why
Power Platform services are being updated to support the 2026 time zone changes in Manitoba, Alberta, and British Columbia. This is a general awareness message to support the changes and complements MC1510951 — Windows updates are available for 2026 time zone changes in Canada.

Rollout schedule
Updates will be delivered by service to support the November 1, 2026, time zone transition. Availability will vary by service.

Power Automate Desktop (RPA): Scheduled trigger updates are planned to roll out November 5 through November 23, 2026.

How does this affect me?
Impact varies by component and time zone configuration:
  • Power Apps (Model-driven Apps): Selecting a new regional time zone may change how existing dates and times are displayed where the old and new rules differ.
  • Power Apps (Canvas Apps): No impact is anticipated, as date-time behavior depends on the device.
  • Power Pages: From November 1, 2026, through December 31, 2026, dates converted by Dataverse and date-based filters may be one hour behind. From 2027, dates and times recorded during past standard-time periods may also display one hour incorrectly. Dates rendered directly in the browser are not affected by the identified issue.
  • Power Automate Process Mining: No impact is anticipated, as date-time behavior depends on the device.
  • Power Automate Desktop (RPA): Beginning November 1, scheduled triggers using the existing Mountain, Pacific, or Central time zones may run one hour off from the intended local time in affected regions. The Get current date and time action also has limitations involving unavailable new time zone options and outdated time zone data.
What action do I need to take?
Keep device operating systems and browsers updated and use the correct local time zone setting. After the relevant service update is available, affected users should select the appropriate new region-specific time zone in their app or service settings, where applicable.

Power Automate Desktop (RPA): Install the October 2026 Windows time zone update on machines running desktop flows. Until the new regional time zones are available for scheduled triggers, use these temporary settings:
  • Alberta: Select “Saskatchewan.”
  • British Columbia: Select “Arizona.”
  • Manitoba: Select “Bogota, Lima, Quito.”

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Teams Default meeting template
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Default Meeting Templates enable IT admins to automatically apply their organization’s preferred meeting options whenever users schedule a Teams meeting through Outlook or Teams calendar. This helps organizations apply meeting options (including protection meeting options) at scale, and reduce the need for organizers to manually configure meeting options.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in early November 2026 and expect to complete by mid November 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

For meeting organizers and co-organizers with a default meeting template applied, their meetings will use the meeting options defined in that template, including protection meeting options. Participants joining those meetings will experience the configured meeting options.

Please note that only organizers and co-organizers with a Teams Premium license can use the default meeting template.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

Default meeting templates help IT admins provide a consistent meeting experience by automatically applying the configured meeting options, including protection meeting options, to scheduled meetings through Outlook or Teams Calendar. Meet Now, Channel Meetings, and Events are out of scope for default meeting template.

  • IT admins first create a custom meeting template and then assign it as the default meeting template. Instructions to create a default meeting template: Create a custom meeting template in Microsoft Teams.
  • Configuration considerations: When configuring the template, admins should review the restrictions and platform limitations associated with the features they enable. Some settings may result in a degraded experience on unsupported platforms.
  • If the default meeting template is removed, meetings will no longer use the meeting options defined by that template. Instead, the meeting options currently applicable to the organizer will take effect.

Recommendation: Do not configure the Copilot meeting policy to “On with saved transcript required.” With this configuration, users may encounter errors with default meeting template. We recommend using an alternative Copilot meeting policy configuration.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Change Optics Report
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Following the public preview announced in MC1301802, the Change Optics report for Exchange Online is now generally available for worldwide tenants. The report helps Exchange administrators identify email traffic that may be affected by upcoming service changes so they can investigate and remediate potential issues before enforcement occurs.

Learn more: The Change Optics report is now generally available in Exchange Online

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): The report is available now.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

The Change Optics report is available in the Exchange Admin Center under Reports > Mail flow > Change Optics Report. The report displays a sample set of messages matching characteristics expected to be affected by Exchange Online transport changes. At GA, the report includes:

  • OMC (Onmicrosoft.com external traffic): Identifies onmicrosoft.com traffic sent externally so organizations can investigate and reduce usage affected by onmicrosoft.com throttling.
  • DRS (Direct Send traffic): Identifies Direct Send traffic received by your tenant, helping administrators identify legitimate senders before enabling Reject Direct Send.

Since Public Preview, we've made improvements to the report thanks to the feedback received.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No action is required. Exchange administrators may want to:

  • Review the Change Optics Report when future Message Center communications reference a Change Optics scenario.
  • Use the OMC scenario to identify and reduce onmicrosoft.com external email usage.
  • Use the DRS scenario to identify Direct Send traffic and prepare for enabling Reject Direct Send where appropriate.
  • Update internal mail flow operational guidance to incorporate Change Optics as part of change preparation.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Copilot for Outlook: New Copilot entry point in Classic Outlook
item.description:

[What and why]

We are updating the entry point for Copilot in Outlook to be more visually appealing and consistent. Located next to the Outlook ribbon, the Copilot entry point makes it easier for users to discover and use Copilot as they work. In addition to chat, it also surfaces contextual, AI-powered recommendations based on the task at hand, such as reading email, composing messages, or managing a calendar. With a single click, users can act on these suggestions to quickly summarize content, draft responses, organize information, and accomplish tasks more efficiently. The experience is designed to bring relevant Copilot capabilities closer to the user's workflow while providing a consistent Copilot experience across Microsoft 365 applications.

This update is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 567007.

[Rollout schedule]

General Availability 

  • Worldwide: Beginning mid-November 2026 (previously late October) and expected to complete by late November 2026 (previously mid-November)
  • GCC and GCC High: Beginning early December 2026 (previously mid-November) and expected to complete by late December 2026 (previously early December)
  • DoD: Beginning early December 2026 (previously mid-November) and expected to complete by late December 2026 (previously early December)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot

What will happen

  • The entry point for Copilot in classic Outlook will be updated and located next to the Outlook ribbon: 
  • Users will continue to have access to the Copilot side pane.
  • This new entry point will surface contextual, AI-powered recommendations based on the task at hand.
  • The feature will be available by default for eligible users with the required Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
  • No existing Copilot licensing requirements or admin settings are changing as part of this update.

[Action required and recommendations]

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Outlook: Change the organizer of meetings
item.description:
Updated October 26, 2026: We have updated the content and timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why:]

Microsoft is introducing Change organizer for eligible Outlook meetings and recurring meeting series. Users can ask another person in their organization to become the organizer, and the selected person must accept before ownership changes. This supports personal and team productivity by maintaining meeting continuity during role changes, leave, and offboarding.

[Rollout Schedule:]

This phase supports non-online meetings:

  • Worldwide: Early November through early December 2026 
  • GCC: Late November through late December 2026 
  • GCC High: Early December through late December 2026 
  • DoD: Early December through late December 2026 

Phase 2 will add eligible online meetings. For Teams meetings, the transfer will generate a new Teams meeting link owned by the new organizer. Phase 2 will also be rolled out along with phase 1 with the same schedule. 

Phase 3 will add transfer support for eligible Teams meeting artifacts, including chat, meeting options, transcripts, recordings, agenda, notes, and attendance reports. Its timing will be announced separately.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  1. Users who organize eligible meetings or recurring series.
  2. Users selected to become a new organizer.
  3. Delegates with permission to edit meetings on another user's primary calendar.
  4. Help desk teams supporting meeting ownership transitions.

Platforms/Services:

  1. Outlook on the web
  2. New Outlook for Windows
  3. Teams Microsoft 365 Calendar
  4. Exchange Online

Classic Outlook for Windows is not supported.

What will happen:

  1. The current organizer can select one person in the same organization or tenant and send an organizer change request.
  2. The meeting remains with the current organizer until the selected person accepts.
  3. The organizer or an authorized delegate can cancel a pending request.
  4. For recurring series, future instances move to the new organizer's calendar. Earlier instances remain with the previous organizer.
  5. Internal Exchange Online attendees receive a silent update and do not need to respond again. Their Reminder, Category, Show As, and Private settings are preserved.
  6. External and on-premises attendees receive a cancellation and a new invitation, which requires a response.
  7. The meeting body, attachments, and sensitivity labels are preserved. The new organizer might require separate access to OneDrive attachments or links.
  8. If the meeting has a Teams meeting, a new Teams meeting link will be generated upon transfer which will be owned by the new organizer.
  9. This feature is enabled by default and requires no tenant configuration. There is no admin setting to control the availability of this feature.

The meeting must be in the future, use a work or school account, and be stored on the organizer's primary calendar. Draft, canceled, encrypted, group calendar, group mailbox, and shared mailbox meetings are not eligible.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No administrative action is required.

  1. Review meeting ownership processes for role changes, leave, and offboarding.
  2. Update internal meeting management and offboarding documentation.
  3. Tell users that the new organizer must accept the request and that the previous organizer is not automatically retained as an attendee.
  4. Advise users that external attendees must respond to a replacement invitation.
  5. Ask users to confirm that the new organizer can access linked OneDrive content.
  6. Review the Microsoft Support article, Change the organizer of a meeting in Outlook.

[Compliance Considerations:]

ConsiderationImpactExplanation
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?YesFuture meeting instances move to the new organizer's calendar and can be managed by that organizer. Earlier recurring instances remain with the previous organizer. Meeting content is preserved, but linked OneDrive content might require separate access.
Does the change provide a new way of communicating between users, tenants, or subscriptions?YesThe feature adds organizer transfer requests within an organization. Internal attendees receive silent updates, while external and on-premises attendees receive a cancellation and replacement invitation.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft 365 Apps: Cloud Update - Export Improvements
item.description:
[What and Why:]

New export improvements are coming to Cloud Update, making it easier for organizations to access and analyze device data. These enhancements will expand export capabilities across Inventory and Cloud Update device views, include additional device and update information, and allow admins to export filtered results so they can focus on the devices most relevant to their needs.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out on early November 2026 and expect to complete by late November 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

We are enhancing export capabilities in Inventory and Cloud Update to make it easier to get the device data you need for reporting, troubleshooting, and sharing with stakeholders. With this update:

  • Inventory export: Export from the Inventory > All devices view will include the Cloud Update Status column, which indicates whether each device is managed, onboarding, excluded, or not eligible for Cloud Update.
  • Cloud Update device export: You can export device data directly from the Current > Devices and Monthly Enterprise > Devices views. Exports include all table columns, such as rollout wave, update status, and errors.
  • Filtered export: You can apply filters to a device view and export only the matching results, such as devices that are not up to date.

This change does not affect which devices appear in Inventory or Cloud Update, or how those devices are managed.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No preparation or configuration is required. Admins can begin using the new export capabilities as they become available.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] AI Builder credits retirement: Prepare to use Copilot Credits
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Microsoft is retiring AI Builder credits and replacing them with Copilot Credits. Organizations using AI Builder must arrange Copilot Credit capacity before their existing AI Builder credit entitlements expire, or sooner if those credits are exhausted, to avoid interruptions.

 AI Builder features are not being retired. They will continue to be supported using Copilot Credits, bringing AI Builder and Microsoft Copilot Studio capabilities onto a common credit-based licensing model.

When this will happen:

  • November 1, 2025: Sales of AI Builder capacity add-ons ended for new customers.
  • November 1, 2026: AI Builder capacity add-ons reach end of life. Credits from active add-on contracts remain usable until those contracts expire.
  • November 1, 2026: New or renewed eligible Power Platform and Dynamics 365 licenses will no longer include seeded AI Builder credits. Seeded credits included with eligible licenses purchased or renewed before this date remain available through the end of the applicable contract term.

November 1, 2026, is not a universal cutoff for existing credits. Your transition deadline depends on when your applicable contracts expire.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): We will begin rolling out on early November 2026 and expect to complete by early November 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

This change affects organizations that use AI Builder credits from capacity add-ons or credits included with eligible Power Platform and Dynamics 365 licenses to run AI Builder features in Power Apps and Power Automate.

  • AI Builder features in Power Apps and Power Automate consume available AI Builder credits first. When those credits are unavailable or exhausted, usage automatically falls back to available Copilot Credits.
  • If neither credit type is available, affected AI Builder runs are blocked, which can interrupt apps, flows, and business processes.
  • AI Builder credits will not automatically convert to Copilot Credits. Consumption rates differ by capability; there is no single conversion ratio.
  • AI Builder features in Copilot Studio already consume Copilot Credits.
  • This change affects licensing, not feature availability. Administrators must ensure sufficient capacity to continue running AI Builder features.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

Admin action is required before November 1, 2026, for organizations with AI Builder capacity add-ons, and before existing credit entitlements expire to prevent disruption.

  1. Review your contracts. Identify when your AI Builder capacity add-ons and licenses providing seeded credits expire. For AI Builder capacity add-ons, turn off automatic renewal in the Microsoft 365 admin center or work with your partner to do so in Partner Center.
  2. Review credit consumption across environments. In the Power Platform admin center, go to Licensing > Capacity add-ons > Download reports > + New > AI Builder. Generate and download the report to review credits consumed by date, user, and environment during the 30 days preceding the selected target date.
  3.  3.** Identify affected workloads.** In the Power Automate portal, select the environment, then go to Automation Center > Monitor > AI Builder activity. Makers can review their own activity for models they can access; users with the System Administrator or System Customizer role can review all activity in the environment. Activity data is also available in the AI Event table in Dataverse.
  4. Plan replacement capacity. Use the AI Builder capability rate table to estimate Copilot Credit requirements. Purchase and make sufficient Copilot Credits available to affected environments before existing AI Builder credit entitlements expire. Do not assume that the same number of Copilot Credits will cover your current AI Builder credit usage.
  5. Notify makers and support teams. Update internal licensing guidance and identify business-critical apps and flows that could be interrupted by insufficient capacity.

Learn more

  • End of AI Builder credits
  • AI Builder licensing overview
  • AI Builder consumption report
  • Monitor AI Builder activity

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Malicious QR code detection in messages
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft Teams is extending malicious URL protection to provide near-real-time detection of malicious destinations embedded in QR codes shared in messages. Teams will analyze QR code destinations to identify potential phishing and fraud threats and display an additional warning when malicious content is detected.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in early November 2026 and expected to complete in mid-November 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users who use Microsoft Teams messaging

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams chats, meeting chats, and channels

What will happen

  • Teams will decode and evaluate QR code destinations in inline images shared in 1:1 chats, group chats, meeting chats, and channels.
  • Detection applies to internal and external communications.
  • Images containing QR codes from external senders are already blurred by default. When Teams identifies a malicious QR code, users will also see the warning, “This message contains a link that might be harmful,” and a “Learn about file and link safety” link.
  • QR code images from internal senders are not blurred by default. The same warning will appear when Teams detects a malicious QR code.
  • For users on Teams mobile in China, QR code images are blurred by default regardless of whether the sender is internal or external, and any messages containing malicious QR code will be blocked.
  • Malicious QR code detection is managed by the existing Malicious URL protection setting.
  • The setting is enabled by default. Organizations with Malicious URL protection enabled will automatically receive malicious QR code detection as the feature rolls out.
  • No separate configuration is available or required for malicious QR code detection.

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin action is required.

Admins can review or change the existing Malicious URL protection setting in Teams admin center > Settings and policies > Messaging Safety.

We recommend that you:

  • Inform users and help desk staff about the additional warning for detected malicious QR codes.
  • Clarify that QR code blurring is a separate precautionary experience and does not mean that Teams has identified a QR code as malicious.
  • Review internal documentation about Teams messaging security and update it if necessary.

Learn more

  • Make sure chats, links, and files are secure in Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Support
  • Malicious URL protection in Microsoft Teams - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

(Both to be updated closer to rollout.)

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Audio Overview Updates
item.description:
Updated October 26, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why:]

Microsoft is rolling out new capabilities in Audio Overview to make it easier to navigate longer content, support enterprise information protection, and create audio overviews from more types of content.

Episodes

For longer and more content-rich notebooks, Audio Overview can organize the discussion into topic-based episodes. This makes it easier for users to navigate the audio and focus on different parts of the content.

Sensitivity labels when saving to OneDrive

Audio Overviews now support Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels when saved to OneDrive. If the source content includes sensitivity labels, the saved Audio Overview inherits the most restrictive label from its sources. Sensitivity labels apply to the saved file in OneDrive. Audio Overviews within the notebook are not yet sensitivity labeled.

More supported content types

Audio Overview can now understand and ground its discussion in additional types of content added to a notebook, including:

  • OneNote pages
  • Loop pages
  • Plain text (.txt) files
  • Emails
  • Teams meetings
  • Teams chats

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in early November 2026 (previously late October) and expect to complete by late November 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Users who create and consume Audio Overviews.
  • Organizations that use Audio Overview with Microsoft 365 content stored or saved in OneDrive.

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Audio Overview
  • OneDrive
  • Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels

What will happen:

  • Users can navigate longer Audio Overviews through topic-based episodes.
  • Users can create Audio Overviews grounded in additional content types, including OneNote pages, Loop pages, .txt files, emails, Teams meetings, and Teams chats.
  • Audio Overviews saved to OneDrive from labeled source content will inherit the most restrictive sensitivity label from the sources.
  • This release does not introduce sensitivity labeling for Audio Overviews while they remain within the notebook.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No admin action is required to prepare for this update. These Audio Overview improvements will roll out automatically to eligible users.

For sensitivity labels, when an Audio Overview is saved to OneDrive from labeled source content, the saved file will automatically inherit the most restrictive sensitivity label from its sources. No additional configuration is required as part of this feature rollout.

[Compliance considerations:]

Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. Audio Overview uses AI capabilities to generate audio grounded in Microsoft 365 content, including additional supported content types.
Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Users can create and navigate Audio Overviews from more supported Microsoft 365 content sources.
Does the change modify, interrupt, or disable Purview capabilities such as Information Protection labels?Yes. Audio Overviews saved to OneDrive from labeled source content inherit the most restrictive sensitivity label from the sources.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: QR code protection for messages from external users
item.description:
Updated October 26, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Microsoft Teams is introducing additional protection for QR codes shared by external users in Teams messages. To help reduce the risk of phishing and fraud, images containing QR codes from external senders will be obscured by default. Users can choose to reveal the image before viewing or scanning the QR code.

This security enhancement promotes safer interactions with content received from external users while maintaining flexibility for trusted communications.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Targeted Release: Beginning in mid-October 2026 (previously early October) and expected to complete in mid-October 2026 (previously early October)
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in late October 2026 (previously mid-October) and expected to complete by late October 2026 (previously mid-October)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations that allow communication with external users in Microsoft Teams.
  • Users who receive Teams messages from external senders.
  • Teams administrators and support teams that manage external collaboration policies.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • Teams desktop
  • Teams web
  • Teams mobile

What will happen

  • Images containing QR codes sent by external users will be blurred by default in Teams messages.
  • Users can reveal the image if they trust the sender and want to view or scan the QR code.
  • The blurred image does not indicate that Microsoft Teams has determined the QR code to be malicious.
  • The protection is applied automatically to QR code images received from external senders.
  • No administrator configuration or policy changes are required.
  • The feature will be enabled by default as part of the rollout.

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin action is required before rollout.

We recommend that administrators:

  • Inform users that QR code images from external senders may appear blurred by default.
  • Remind users to verify the sender before revealing or scanning QR codes.
  • Review existing user education materials related to phishing awareness, QR code safety, and external collaboration.
  • Update internal help desk documentation to reflect the new user experience.

Learn more:

  • QR code obscuring in Microsoft Teams - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn
  • Make sure chats, links, and files are secure in Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Support

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Entra: Users can register a passkey or passwordless sign-in as their first multifactor authentication method
item.description:
Updated October 26, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Users will soon be able to register a passkey as their first multifactor authentication method. Previously, people had to set up an alternate MFA method like SMS or Voice before they could add a passkey (FIDO2), Windows Hello for Business, macOS Platform SSO. That extra step pushed users toward weaker methods and slowed the move to phishing-resistant sign-in. Now password-only users can go straight to a passkey, making it easier to adopt strong authentication from day one. As part of this work, we will also be enabling Authenticator App passwordless sign-in to be a user's first registered MFA method. 

[Rollout schedule]

This feature will roll out in phases: 

Phase 1: Support for synced passkeys, Microsoft Entra passkeys on Windows, and FIDO2 security keys.  

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): We will begin rolling out in early November 2026 (previously late October) and expect to complete by early January 2027 (previously late November 2026). 

Phase 2: Support for Windows Hello for Business, macOS Platform SSO, Authenticator App passkey, and Authenticator App passwordless sign-in. 

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): We will begin rolling out in early January 2026 and expect to complete by late February 2027. 

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users who have not yet registered a multifactor authentication method
  • Identity and security administrators responsible for authentication onboarding and registration policies

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • Passkeys (FIDO2)
  • Windows Hello for Business
  • macOS Platform SSO
  • Microsoft Authenticator passwordless sign-in

What will happen

  • Password-only users will be able to register passkeys or passwordless sign-in as their first MFA method.
  • Users will no longer need to register a method such as SMS or voice before registering a passkey (FIDO2), Windows Hello for Business, macOS Platform SSO, or Authenticator passwordless sign-in.
  • Organizations may see reduced registration friction and increased adoption of phishing-resistant authentication methods.
  • Users who are enabled for passkeys will be prompted to register a passkey by default when completing applicable registration experiences, including those triggered by multifactor authentication (MFA) enforcement and Conditional Access authentication strengths. Security Defaults MFA registration prompts will adopt this experience in January–February 2027.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required for this change.

We recommend that administrators:

  • Review Conditional Access policies related to security information registration.
  • Consider requiring MFA to register security information if additional verification is required by your organization.
  • Review your user onboarding and registration guidance and update it as needed to reflect that eligible users may be prompted to register a passkey by default.

Learn more 

  • (To be updated closer to rollout) Register a synced passkey (FIDO2) | Authentication | Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. Administrators can control which authentication methods users are allowed to register through existing Microsoft Entra authentication method policies and Conditional Access policies.
Does the change affect access or authentication controls?Yes. The update changes how users register multifactor authentication methods by allowing eligible users to register supported passkeys or passwordless authentication methods as their first MFA method.
Can administrators govern the feature through existing Microsoft Entra controls?Yes. Administrators retain control over the feature through Microsoft Entra authentication method policies and Conditional Access configurations.

item.title: [preventOrFixIssue] Update to MC1510951: Canada 2026 time zone changes — Microsoft 365 impact and required admin actions
item.description:
This post updates MC1510951 ((Updated) Windows updates are available for 2026 time zone changes in Canada, posted October 16, 2026).

On November 1, 2026, affected locations in British Columbia, Alberta, and Manitoba will not move clocks back and will remain on UTC-07:00, UTC-06:00, and UTC-05:00 respectively. Affected locations in the Northwest Territories (including Yellowknife and Inuvik) align with the Alberta change, and Northwestern Ontario aligns with the Manitoba change.

Windows and Microsoft 365 services depend on updated time zone definitions for correct scheduling and display behavior.

How this affects your organization

Confirmed impact

  1. Outlook and Exchange Online (calendar): Users must move to the new time zone. Existing events do not migrate automatically. Recurring meetings require additional review.
  2. Microsoft Teams Rooms on Windows: Some devices may display time one hour behind Windows until Edge/WebView2 is updated.

Potential impact (under validation)

item.title: [planForChange] Dynamics 365 and Power Platform– Information about storage validation for Dataverse-only tenants
item.description:
Beginning November 9, 2026, we are introducing staged storage validation for supported Dynamics 365 applications. The change gives administrators clearer visibility into storage use, advance notice of potential restrictions, and several ways to remain within capacity, including removing unneeded data, adding capacity, or enabling pay-as-you-go for sandbox environments.

If no corrective action is initiated after repeated notifications, when a tenant exceeds its entitled Database, File, or Log capacity, environment creation, copy, restore, and recover operations will be restricted immediately. If the overage remains unresolved, sandbox environments that do not have pay-as-you-go billing enabled will enter Administration mode after 30 days of remaining over capacity, allowing access only to administrators. After 90 days from the date the tenant exceeds capacity, affected sandbox environments will be disabled and will no longer be accessible to users. During this phase customers can contact Microsoft Support for the sole purpose of directing data export options, if needed.

Production environments are not subject to administration mode and disabled stage restrictions and will remain accessible. However, environment creation, copy, restore, and recover operations for sandbox or production type environments will remain blocked while the tenant is over capacity.

Deployment Timeline:
  • Rollout begins: November 9, 2026
  • Rollout completion: December 14, 2026
How does this affect me?
The Dataverse storage validation applies only to Dataverse-only tenants without Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations environment(s) or consumption. The following products are included in the storage validation rollout:
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Service
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Field Service
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Voice
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Contact Center
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Project Operations (Dataverse deployments)
If your tenant exceeds its entitled storage capacity, the following lifecycle applies:

Stage Timing Impact
1. Restricted When the tenant first exceeds its entitled storage capacity, known as time zero (T0) Environment creation, copy, restore, and recover operations for sandbox and production type environments are blocked immediately when the tenant exceeds its entitled capacity.
2. Administration mode After 30 unresolved days from T0 Only administrators can sign in to *affected sandbox environments. All other users are blocked from accessing the environment.
3. Disabled After 90 unresolved days from T0 All users, including administrators, are blocked from accessing *affected sandbox environments; the environment data is retained and remains available for recovery after remediation. During this phase, customers can contact Microsoft Support for the sole purpose of directing data export options, if needed. All other mechanisms designed to resolve overage are also available to customers at this phase.

Sandbox environments with active pay-as-you-go billing do not progress through the storage overage lifecycle even if the tenant remains over storage capacity. Other *affected sandbox environments in the tenant may still be affected with restrictions.

We will provide notifications that include the tenant’s current storage status, the date it first exceeded capacity, its current lifecycle stage, future restrictions, and recommended remediation actions.

Admins can exit Administration Mode at any time; however, the overage lifecycle continues as long as the tenant remains over its entitled storage capacity. Once the tenant returns below 100%, no further restrictions are applied. Environments do not automatically return to their previous state; admins must manually exit Administration Mode or re-enable them, as applicable. Processing time may vary depending on the remediation method used.

Sandbox environments with active pay-as-you-go billing are excluded from the overage lifecycle even if the tenant remains over storage capacity.

What action do I need to take?
Review your environment(s) and perform the following actions before November 9, 2026:
  • Review Database, File, and Log capacity in the Power Platform admin center.
  • Remove or archive data that is no longer needed.
  • Establish data governance policies in your environment to help prevent future storage overages.
  • Purchase additional capacity or configure pay-as-you-go.
  • Invite makers and users to become aware of these potential restrictions and to notify administrators about possible areas of adjustment.
  • Review your release activities that depend on sandbox availability, and plan accordingly.
For additional information, please visit the following articles:
  • What happens when my organization exceeds storage capacity?
  • Dataverse capacity-based storage details
  • Manage data with Dataverse governance policies
  • Free up storage space
  • Add more Dataverse capacity
  • Configure pay-as-you-go in your environment
  • What environments consume tenant capacity
  • Power Platform licensing guidance
*Affected environments: Sandbox environments that do not have pay-as-you-go enabled. Any references to affected environments in this message apply exclusively to those sandbox environments

item.title: [stayInformed] Teams admin center - Intelligent insights for meeting quality

  • Identify meeting-quality hotspots across locations and public IPs and see how many users are affected.
  • Review quality trends to understand how meeting quality has changed over time.
  • Understand likely root causes across network factors such as bandwidth, Wi-Fi, VPN and proxy; compute factors such as CPU, memory and client; and devices such as microphones, cameras and speakers.

Insights are refreshed daily and use machine learning to dynamically evaluate what constitutes anomalous behavior, so administrators don’t need to configure thresholds.

The insights use meeting data across the tenant and supported clients and platforms. They do not include meeting telemetry from SIP phones or telemetry from PSTN and peer-to-peer calls.

  • A Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
  • A spending policy.

  • Cloud coding sessions are enabled on web and PC for eligible users with a Copilot spending policy.
  • Local coding sessions are disabled by default. Admins can allow local coding on PC by setting Code execution location to Cloud and local in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Users covered by a spending policy where the setting "Allow new Agents and services as they become available" is enabled automatically receive access to Code through that spending policy.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Phishing detection for messaging

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Entra: Choose your own telephony provider for SMS and voice authentication
item.description:
[What and why]

Starting October 30, 2026, Microsoft Entra ID will make Choose Your Own Telephony Provider (CYOT) generally available. CYOT enables organizations to use a supported third-party telecommunications provider for SMS and voice authentication. Organizations select a supported provider through Microsoft Security Store and manage their commercial relationship directly with the provider.

Microsoft recommends phishing-resistant authentication methods, such as passkeys, instead of SMS or voice authentication. Organizations should use a telephony provider only for user populations that have a business, regulatory, or technical requirement for telephony-based authentication. 

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning October 30, 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations with users who require SMS or voice authentication for business, regulatory, or technical reasons

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • Microsoft Security Store

What will happen

  • Starting October 30, 2026, organizations can choose to configure a supported telephony provider for SMS and voice authentication.
  • Your selected provider will deliver the SMS messages or voice calls users need to complete authentication.
  • Microsoft Entra ID will continue to enforce authentication method policies and coordinate the authentication experience.
  • Your organization will manage its commercial relationship with the selected provider.
  • Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication is scheduled to be retired on February 1, 2027, for all users except Global Administrators and external users. The retirement date for Global Administrators and external users is July 1, 2027. Internal guest users remain subject to the February 1, 2027 retirement date.
  • After the applicable retirement date, users whose only available MFA method is SMS or voice must register a passkey during sign-in unless the organization has configured a supported telephony provider. This registration prompt is blocking.

[Action required and recommendations]

If your organization plans to adopt CYOT:

  • Identify affected users. Determine which users have a documented business, regulatory, or technical requirement for SMS or voice authentication.
  • Evaluate phishing-resistant alternatives. Confirm that a phishing-resistant authentication method does not meet the requirements for those users.
  • Review supported telephony providers. Compare providers based on geographic coverage, supported delivery channels, pricing, support, security, and compliance capabilities.
  • Review organizational requirements. Work with the appropriate teams to review procurement, privacy, and regulatory requirements before selecting a provider.
  • Plan your transition. Review Passkeys by default and retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication and plan your transition based on the retirement date applicable to each user population.
  • Validate purchasing requirements. Review Purchase a SaaS solution and deploy a linked solution. Purchasing through Security Store requires an Azure billing subscription and resource group, plus the appropriate Azure subscription role.
  • Estimate costs. Review provider pricing and expected Azure infrastructure charges before deployment.

Learn more

  • Choose a telephony provider for SMS and voice authentication - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn
  • Estimate telephony provider and Azure hosting costs: ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample/docs/COST-CALCULATOR.md at main · Azure-Samples/ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample
  • Passkeys by default and retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn
  • Purchase and deploy a SaaS solution from Security Store - Microsoft Security Store | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change add any integration to third-party software products, and if so, what?Yes. The change enables organizations to use a supported third-party telephony provider for SMS and voice authentication. Organizations select a provider through Microsoft Security Store, and the selected provider delivers the SMS messages or voice calls used for authentication.
